chunks: This is what is agreed upon with regards to his dictation briefly describing the religion of the Imamiyya.
And I will dictate an explanation and an interpretation of it if Allah — Mighty is His name — eases my return from my destination to Nishapur, God-willingly.

key_terms.إملاء: Dictation (imla') — the classical method of scholarly transmission in which a teacher dictates to students who write it down
key_terms.الإمامية: The Imamiyya — the Twelver Shia community, those who believe in twelve Imams from the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.العجلة: Haste (al-'ajala) — indicating the text was composed quickly, not with the full care the author intended
key_terms.شرح وتفسير: Explanation and interpretation — the promised fuller commentary that al-Saduq planned for his return

ai.seo_question: What did Shaykh al-Saduq say about his description of the Imami religion?
ai.summary: This closing statement is an authorial note by Shaykh al-Saduq, written during the session of the Ninety-Third Assembly on Friday, 13th Sha'ban, 368 AH. Al-Saduq acknowledges that what he has dictated thus far is a brief summary of the Imami creed, composed hastily, and promises to provide a more thorough explanation and commentary upon his return to Nishapur. This note reveals that al-Saduq was traveling at the time and composed this brief creedal statement as a temporary summary, intending to expand it later, demonstrating the scholarly practice of summarizing beliefs for an audience while on journey.

en.bilal-muhammad: This is what is agreed upon with regards to his dictation briefly describing the religion of the Imamiyya.
I will dictate an explanation and an interpretation of it if Allah eases my return from my destination to Nishapur, God-willingly.
